units.2 Kings 23:30: His servants transported him dead from Mageddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his grave in David’s city. The people of the land took Joachas son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in his father’s place.
units.2 Kings 23:31: Joachas was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amital daughter of Jeremiah, from Lemna.
units.2 Kings 23:32: He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his fathers had done.
units.2 Kings 23:33: Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in Emath’s land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.
units.2 Kings 23:34: Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim, son of Josiah king of Judah, king over them in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Joakim. He took Joachas and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
units.2 Kings 23:35: Joakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but assessed the land to provide the silver at Pharaoh’s command. Each according to his assessment, they gave the silver and gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Nechao.
units.James 5:1: Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
units.James 5:2: Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
units.James 5:3: Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
units.James 5:4: Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
units.James 5:5: You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.
units.James 5:6: You condemned; you murdered the righteous one. He does not oppose you.
units.Leviticus 19:11: You shall not steal. You shall not lie. No one shall defraud his neighbour.
units.Leviticus 19:12: And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
units.Leviticus 19:13: You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
units.Leviticus 19:14: You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
units.Leviticus 19:15: You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
units.Haggai 1:1: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
units.Haggai 1:2: ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”
units.Haggai 1:3: The word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
units.Haggai 1:4: “Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?
units.Haggai 1:5: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.
units.Haggai 1:6: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
units.Proverbs 29:4: A righteous king raises up a country, but a lawless man tears it down.
units.Proverbs 29:14: When a king judges the poor in truth, his throne will be established as a testimony.
units.Micah 3:9: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,
units.Micah 3:10: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!
units.Micah 3:11: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
units.Micah 3:12: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.
units.Jeremiah 43:27: After the king burned the roll—all the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth—the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
units.Jeremiah 43:28: Take another roll again and write all the words that were on the roll which King Jehoiakim burned.
units.Jeremiah 43:29: Say, Thus said the Lord: You burned this roll, saying, Why did you write in it that Babylon’s king will certainly enter and destroy this land, and people and animals will cease from it?
units.Jeremiah 43:30: Therefore thus said the Lord concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one sitting on David’s throne. His carcass will be thrown out in the day’s heat and the night’s frost.
units.Jeremiah 43:31: I will visit him, his family, and his servants, and bring upon them, Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and Judah’s land all the calamities I pronounced to them, but they did not listen.
units.Jeremiah 43:32: Baruch took another roll and wrote on it, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words of the document Jehoiakim burned. Still more words like these were added to it.
units.Lamentations 1:1: After Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem laid waste, Jeremiah sat weeping and lamented this lament over Jerusalem, saying: How the city once full of peoples sat alone! She has become like a widow, she who was populous among the nations. A ruler among the regions has become subject to tribute.
units.Lamentations 1:2: Weeping, she wept in the night, her tears upon her cheeks. Among all those who love her there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have dealt faithlessly with her; they have become her enemies.
units.Lamentations 1:3: Judea was deported because of her humiliation and her great slavery. She dwelt among the nations; she found no rest. All her pursuers overtook her among those who afflicted her.
units.Jeremiah 10:19: Woe for your crushing! Your wound is painful. And I said: Truly this is my wound, and it has seized me.
units.Jeremiah 10:20: My tent suffered misery and perished, and all my tent coverings were torn apart. My sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my coverings.
units.Jeremiah 10:21: For the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek the Lord; therefore all the pasture did not perceive, and they were scattered.
units.Jeremiah 10:22: A sound of a report—behold, it comes! And a great shaking from the northern land, to lay Judah’s cities waste and make them a resting place for ostriches.
units.Micah 4:9: And now why have you experienced calamities? Did you have no king? Has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?
units.Micah 4:10: Labor in birth, be courageous and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth! For now you will go out from the city, camp in the plain and come as far as Babylon. From there He will rescue you, and from there the Lord your God will redeem you from your enemies’ hand.
units.Haggai 2:20: The word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai the prophet on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:
units.Haggai 2:21: “Speak to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, saying: I am shaking heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land,
units.Haggai 2:22: and I will overturn the thrones of kings and destroy the strength of the kings of the nations. I will overturn chariots and riders; horses and their riders will fall, each with a sword against his brother.
units.Haggai 2:23: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will take you, Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, My servant, says the Lord, and make you like a signet, for I have chosen you, says the Lord Almighty.”
units.2 Kings 24:8: Joakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nestha daughter of Ellanathan, from Jerusalem.
units.2 Kings 24:9: He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his father had done.
units.2 Kings 24:10: At that time Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
units.2 Kings 24:11: Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon entered the city while his servants were besieging it.
units.2 Kings 24:12: Joakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, his servants, his mother, his rulers, and his eunuchs. The king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
units.2 Kings 24:13: He brought out from there all the treasures of the Lord’s house and the treasures of the king’s house. He cut apart all the gold vessels Solomon king of Israel had made in the Lord’s sanctuary, according to the Lord’s word.
units.2 Kings 24:14: He deported Jerusalem, all the rulers, and the mighty in strength, taking ten thousand captives, and every craftsman and one who shuts up. None remained except the land’s poor.
units.2 Kings 24:15: He deported Joakim to Babylon, along with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, and his eunuchs. He led the land’s powerful men into deportation from Jerusalem to Babylon,
units.2 Kings 24:16: and all the men of the force, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and those who shut up, one thousand—all mighty men who waged war. The king of Babylon brought them into deportation to Babylon.
units.2 Kings 24:17: The king of Babylon made Maththanias, his son, king in his place and gave him the name Sedekias.

units.Hosea 8:6: in Israel? A craftsman made it, and it is no god, because your calf was leading people astray, Samaria.
units.Hosea 8:7: Because they sowed wind-blasted things, their overthrow will receive them: a sheaf without strength to make flour. Even if it does make flour, foreigners will devour it.
units.Hosea 8:8: Israel was swallowed up; now he became among the nations like a useless vessel.
units.Hosea 8:9: Because they went up to the Assyrians; Ephraim flourished by himself, and they loved gifts.
units.Hosea 8:10: Therefore they will be handed over among the nations. Now I will receive them, and they will pause a little from anointing a king and rulers.
units.Deuteronomy 32:1: Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
units.Deuteronomy 32:2: Let my utterance be awaited as the rain, and let my words descend as the dew, as a shower upon the grass, and as snow upon the herbage.
units.Deuteronomy 32:3: For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
units.Deuteronomy 32:4: God—true are His works, and all His ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no unrighteousness; righteous and holy is the Lord.
units.Matthew 1:1: A book of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
units.Matthew 1:2: Abraham begot Isaac; and Isaac begot Jacob; and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers;
units.Matthew 1:3: Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez begot Hezron; Hezron begot Ram;
units.Matthew 1:4: Ram begot Amminadab; Amminadab begot Nahshon; Nahshon begot Salmon;
units.Matthew 1:5: Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab; Boaz begot Obed by Ruth; Obed begot Jesse;
units.Matthew 1:6: Jesse begot David the king. David begot Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
units.Matthew 1:7: Solomon begot Rehoboam; Rehoboam begot Abijah; Abijah begot Asaph;
units.Matthew 1:8: Asaph begot Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat begot Joram; Joram begot Uzziah;
units.Matthew 1:9: Uzziah begot Jotham; Jotham begot Ahaz; Ahaz begot Hezekiah;
units.Matthew 1:10: Hezekiah begot Manasseh; Manasseh begot Amos; Amos begot Josiah;
units.Matthew 1:11: Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers at the deportation to Babylon.
units.Matthew 1:12: After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begot Shealtiel; Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel;
units.Matthew 1:13: Zerubbabel begot Abiud; Abiud begot Eliakim; Eliakim begot Azor;
units.Matthew 1:14: Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud;
units.Matthew 1:15: Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
units.Matthew 1:16: and Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
units.Matthew 1:17: So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.
units.Ezekiel 34:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 34:2: “Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy and say to the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O shepherds of Israel, surely shepherds do not feed themselves? Do shepherds not feed the sheep?
units.Ezekiel 34:3: Behold, you consume the milk, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fattened animal, but you do not feed My sheep.
units.Ezekiel 34:4: You have not strengthened the weak, restored the sick to health, bound up the broken, brought back the wandering or sought the lost. You have worn down the strong with toil.
units.Ezekiel 34:5: My sheep scattered because there were no shepherds and became food for all the field’s beasts.
units.Ezekiel 34:6: My sheep scattered on every mountain and upon every high hill, and scattered over the whole face of the earth. There was no one seeking them out or turning them back.
units.Ezekiel 34:7: Therefore, shepherds, hear the Lord’s word:
units.Ezekiel 34:8: I live, says the Lord, the Lord: surely because My sheep became plunder and My sheep became food for all the plain’s beasts for lack of shepherds, and the shepherds did not seek out My sheep but fed themselves and did not feed My sheep—
units.Ezekiel 34:10: thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against the shepherds. I will require My sheep from their hands and turn them aside from shepherding My sheep. The shepherds will no longer feed them. I will rescue My sheep from their mouth, and they will no longer be food for them.
units.Ezekiel 34:11: For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek out My sheep and visit them.
units.Ezekiel 34:12: As a shepherd seeks his flock on a day when there is gloom and cloud among separated sheep, so I will seek out My sheep and drive them away from every place where they scattered on a day of cloud and gloom.
units.Ezekiel 34:13: I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.
units.Ezekiel 34:14: I will feed them in good pasture, and their folds will be upon Israel’s high mountain. There they will lie down, there rest in good delight, and graze in rich pasture upon Israel’s mountains.
units.Ezekiel 34:15: I Myself will feed My sheep and give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
units.Ezekiel 34:16: I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.
units.Ezekiel 34:23: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.
units.Ezekiel 34:24: I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
units.Ezekiel 34:25: I will make a covenant of peace with David and remove harmful beasts from the land. They will dwell in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.
units.Ezekiel 34:26: I will place them around My mountain and give you rain, rain of blessing.
units.Ezekiel 34:27: The trees in the plain will give their fruit, and the land will give its strength. They will dwell upon their land in hope of peace and know that I am the Lord when I shatter their yoke. I will rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.

units.Ezekiel 13:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 13:2: “Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s prophets; you will prophesy and say to them, ‘Hear the Lord’s word!
units.Ezekiel 13:3: Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and see nothing at all!
units.Ezekiel 13:4: Your prophets, Israel, are like foxes in the wildernesses.
units.Ezekiel 13:5: They did not stand in a firm position, and they gathered flocks against the house of Israel. Those saying, ‘On the Lord’s day,’ did not rise.
units.Ezekiel 13:6: They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
units.Ezekiel 13:7: Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
units.Ezekiel 13:8: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,
units.Ezekiel 13:9: and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 13:10: Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,
units.Ezekiel 13:11: say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.
units.Ezekiel 13:12: And behold, the wall has fallen! Will they not say to you, ‘Where is your coating with which you coated it?’
units.Ezekiel 13:13: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will unleash an upending blast with wrath; a flooding downpour will come in My anger, and I will bring the projectile stones in wrath for complete destruction,
units.Ezekiel 13:14: and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 13:15: I will complete My wrath upon the wall and those coating it, and it will fall. I said to you, ‘There is no wall, nor those coating it—
units.Ezekiel 13:16: the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see peace for her, when there is no peace,’ says the Lord.’
units.Ezekiel 13:17: And you, son of man, set your face firmly against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart, and prophesy against them,
units.Ezekiel 13:18: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Woe to the women sewing cushions upon every elbow of an arm and making coverings upon every head of every age, to distort lives! The lives of My people were distorted, and they were preserving lives.
units.Ezekiel 13:19: They were profaning Me among My people for a handful of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death lives that ought not die and preserving lives that ought not live, as you uttered things to a people listening to vain pronouncements.
units.Ezekiel 13:20: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against your cushions, on which you entangle lives. I will tear them from your arms and send the lives out—their lives that you twist away—into dispersion.
units.Ezekiel 13:21: I will tear your coverings and rescue My people from your hand. They will no longer be in your hands for entanglement, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 13:22: Because you distorted the righteous person’s heart unjustly, though I was not distorting him, and strengthened the lawless person’s hands so that he does not turn at all from his evil way and live,
units.Ezekiel 13:23: therefore you certainly will no longer see false things or divine divinations. I will rescue My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
units.Isaiah 1:1: The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
units.Isaiah 1:2: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.

units.Isaiah 1:5: Why should you be struck again as you add lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart in grief.

units.Isaiah 1:8: Daughter Zion will be left like a tent in a vineyard, like a fruit-watcher’s shelter in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.

units.1 Kings 22:13: The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Behold, all the prophets speak favorable things about the king with one mouth. Please let your words be like the words of one of them, and speak favorably.”

units.Jeremiah 18:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
units.Jeremiah 18:2: Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.
units.Jeremiah 18:3: And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones.
units.Jeremiah 18:4: And the vessel he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as pleased him to make.
units.Jeremiah 18:5: And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
units.Jeremiah 18:6: Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands.
units.Jeremiah 18:7: At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,
units.Jeremiah 18:8: and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.
units.Jeremiah 18:9: And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,
units.Jeremiah 18:10: and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.
units.Jeremiah 18:11: And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.
units.Jeremiah 18:12: And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.
units.Jeremiah 18:13: Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among the nations: Who heard such horrifying things that virgin Israel committed so greatly?
units.Jeremiah 18:14: Will breasts fail from a rock, or snow from Lebanon? Will water borne violently by wind turn aside?
units.Jeremiah 18:15: Because My people forgot Me, they burned incense in vain; and they will become weak in their ways, the age-old tracks, to step upon paths having no road for travel,
units.Jeremiah 18:16: to make their land a ruin and an eternal hissing; all who pass through it will be astonished and shake their head.
units.Jeremiah 18:17: Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them their day of destruction.
units.Jeremiah 18:18: And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.
units.Jeremiah 18:19: Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.
units.Jeremiah 18:20: Is evil repaid for good things? For they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me. Remember my standing before Thee to speak good things for them, to turn Thy fury from them.
units.Jeremiah 18:21: Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.
units.Jeremiah 18:22: Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.
units.Jeremiah 18:23: And Thou, Lord, knewest all their counsel against me for death. Do not acquit their injustices or erase their sins from before Thee. Let their weakness be before Thee; act among them in the time of Thy fury.
units.Jeremiah 19:1: Then the Lord said to me: Go and acquire a molded earthenware jar, and bring some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests.
units.Jeremiah 19:2: And go out to the burial ground of the sons of their children, which is before the Charsith Gate, and read there all the words that I speak to you.
units.Jeremiah 19:3: And say to them: Hear the Lord’s word, kings of Judah, men of Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and those entering these gates. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place, so that both ears of everyone hearing them will ring.
units.Jeremiah 19:4: Because they abandoned Me and alienated this place, burning incense in it to foreign gods whom neither they nor their fathers knew; and Judah’s kings filled this place with innocent blood,
units.Jeremiah 19:5: and built high places for Baal to burn their sons in fire, things I did not command or speak of or conceive in My heart.
units.Jeremiah 19:6: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and this place will no longer be called Collapse or the Burial Ground of the Son of Hinnom, but the Burial Ground of Slaughter.
units.Jeremiah 19:7: And I will slaughter Judah’s counsel and Jerusalem’s counsel in this place, and cast them down by the sword before their enemies and into the hands of those seeking their lives. I will give their dead as food to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth.
units.Jeremiah 19:8: And I will make this city a ruin and a hissing. Everyone passing through it will look gloomy and hiss over its whole wound.
units.Jeremiah 19:9: And they will eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and each will eat his neighbor’s flesh in the encirclement and siege with which their enemies will besiege them.
units.Jeremiah 19:10: And smash the jar before the eyes of the men going out with you,
units.Jeremiah 19:11: and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.
units.Jeremiah 19:12: This is what I will do, says the Lord, to this place and its inhabitants, so that this city is made like the collapsing place.
units.Jeremiah 19:13: And Jerusalem’s houses and the houses of Judah’s kings will be like the collapsing place of uncleannesses, in all the houses where they burned incense upon their roofs to all the host of the heavens and poured drink offerings to foreign gods.
units.Jeremiah 19:14: And Jeremiah came from Collapse, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy, stood in the courtyard of the Lord’s house, and said to all the people:
units.Jeremiah 19:15: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon this city, all its towns, and its villages all the evils I spoke against it, because they hardened their necks so as not to listen to My words.
units.Jeremiah 20:1: And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who had been appointed leader of the Lord’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
units.Jeremiah 20:2: And he struck him and put him into the trap, which was at the gate of the separated upper house that was in the Lord’s house.
units.Jeremiah 20:3: And Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the trap, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has called your name not Pashhur but Migrant.
units.Jeremiah 20:4: Because thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving you to migration with all your friends. They will fall by their enemies’ sword, and your eyes will see. I will give you and all Judah into the hands of Babylon’s king, and they will deport them and cut them down with swords.
units.Jeremiah 20:5: And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 20:6: And you and all who dwell in your house will go into captivity. In Babylon you will die and there be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.
units.Jeremiah 20:7: Thou didst deceive me, Lord, and I was deceived. Thou tookest hold and didst prevail. I became a laughingstock; all day I continued being mocked.
units.Jeremiah 20:8: Because I will laugh with my bitter word; I will call upon rejection and misery, because the Lord’s word became a reproach and a derision to me all day long.
units.Jeremiah 20:9: And I said: I will certainly not name the Lord’s name or speak in His name again. And it became like a burning fire blazing in my bones; I am weakened on every side and cannot bear it.
units.Jeremiah 20:10: Because I heard the reproach of many gathering all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all you men who are his friends! Watch his purpose, to see whether he will be deceived and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.
units.Jeremiah 20:11: And the Lord is with me like a strong fighter. Therefore they pursued and could not understand; they were greatly shamed, because they did not understand their dishonors, which will never be forgotten.
units.Jeremiah 20:12: Lord, testing righteous things, understanding kidneys and hearts: May I see the vengeance from Thee among them, because to Thee I disclosed my defenses.
units.Jeremiah 20:13: Sing to the Lord; praise Him, because He rescued a poor person’s life from the hand of those doing evil.
units.Jeremiah 20:14: Accursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day my mother bore me not be a day to pray for!
units.Jeremiah 20:15: Accursed be the man who brought my father good news, saying, A boy has been born to you!—rejoicing.
units.Jeremiah 20:16: Let that man be like the cities the Lord overthrew in fury without changing His mind. Let him hear a cry in the morning and a battle shout at noon,
units.Jeremiah 20:17: because he did not kill me in my mother’s womb, so that my mother would have become my tomb and the womb one of everlasting conception.
units.Jeremiah 20:18: Why did I come out from the womb to see labors and pains, and have my days continue in shame?
units.Jeremiah 21:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:
units.Jeremiah 21:2: Ask the Lord about us, because Babylon’s king has come against us, whether the Lord will act according to all His wonders, so that he goes away from us.
units.Jeremiah 21:3: And Jeremiah said to them: Say this to Zedekiah king of Judah:
units.Jeremiah 21:4: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am turning the weapons of war with which you fight the Chaldeans who have shut you in outside the wall into this city,
units.Jeremiah 21:5: and I Myself will fight you with outstretched hand and mighty arm, with fury, anger, and great indignation.
units.Jeremiah 21:6: And I will strike all this city’s inhabitants, the people and the livestock, with a great death, and they will die.
units.Jeremiah 21:7: And afterward—thus says the Lord—I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, and the people remaining in this city after death, famine, and sword into the hands of their enemies who seek their lives. They will cut them down with the sword’s edge. I will not spare them or have compassion on them.
units.Jeremiah 21:8: And say to this people: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have set before your face the way of life and the way of death.
units.Jeremiah 21:9: Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.
units.Jeremiah 21:10: Because I have fixed My face upon this city for evils and not for good things. It will be handed into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will burn it down with fire.
units.Jeremiah 21:11: House of Judah’s king, hear the Lord’s word.
units.Jeremiah 21:12: House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.
units.Jeremiah 21:13: Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Sor, the level land, you who say, Who will frighten us? Or who will enter our dwelling?
units.Jeremiah 21:14: And I will kindle a fire in her woodland, and it will consume everything around her.
units.Jeremiah 22:1: Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,
units.Jeremiah 22:2: and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.
units.Jeremiah 22:3: Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.
units.Jeremiah 22:4: Because if you truly carry out this word, kings sitting upon David’s throne and riding chariots and horses will enter this house’s gates—they, their servants, and their people.
units.Jeremiah 22:5: But if you do not carry out these words, I swear by Myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a desolation.
units.Jeremiah 22:6: Because thus says the Lord against the house of Judah’s king: You are Gilead to Me, the head of Lebanon; surely I will make you a wilderness, cities that will not be inhabited.
units.Jeremiah 22:7: And I will bring against you a destroying man and his axe, and they will cut down your chosen cedars and cast them into the fire.
units.Jeremiah 22:8: And nations will pass through this city, and each will say to his neighbor: Why did the Lord act this way toward this great city?
units.Jeremiah 22:9: And they will say: Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down to foreign gods, and served them.
units.Jeremiah 22:10: Do not weep for the dead or lament him; weep bitterly for the one going out, because he will never return or see his homeland.
units.Jeremiah 22:11: Because thus says the Lord concerning Shallum son of Josiah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah and went out from this place: He will not return there again,
units.Jeremiah 22:12: but in the place where I deported him, there he will die, and he will never see this land again.
units.Jeremiah 22:13: O you who build your house without righteousness and your upper rooms without judgment! He works through his neighbor without payment and will not give him his wages.
units.Jeremiah 22:14: You built yourself a well-proportioned house, airy upper rooms set apart by windows, paneled with cedar and painted with red ocher.
units.Jeremiah 22:15: Will you reign because you are provoked in Ahaz your father? They will not eat or drink. It was better for you to do judgment and good righteousness.
units.Jeremiah 22:16: They did not know; they did not judge a case for the lowly or a case for the poor. Is this not your failing to know Me? says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 22:17: Behold, neither your eyes nor your heart are good; instead they are directed toward your greed, innocent blood to shed it, wrongdoing, and murder to commit it.
units.Jeremiah 22:18: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: Woe upon this man! They will certainly not mourn him, O brother! Nor will they weep for him, Alas, lord!
units.Jeremiah 22:19: He will be buried with a donkey’s burial; swept up, he will be thrown beyond Jerusalem’s gate.
units.Jeremiah 22:20: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan and shout to the far side of the sea, because all your lovers have been shattered.
units.Jeremiah 22:21: I spoke to you in your falling away, and you said, I will not listen. This is your way from your youth: you did not hear My voice.
units.Jeremiah 22:22: Wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go out in captivity. Then you will be ashamed and dishonored because of all who love you.
units.Jeremiah 22:23: You who dwell in Lebanon and nest among the cedars will groan when pangs come upon you like those of a woman giving birth.
units.Jeremiah 22:24: As I live, says the Lord, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, becomes a signet on My right hand, I will pull you off from there,
units.Jeremiah 22:25: and hand you into the hands of those seeking your life, those before whom you are afraid, into the hands of the Chaldeans.
units.Jeremiah 22:26: And I will cast you and your mother who bore you into a land where you were not born, and there you both will die.
units.Jeremiah 22:27: But to the land for which they pray in their souls, they will certainly not return.
units.Jeremiah 22:28: Jeconiah was dishonored like a vessel for which there is no use, because he was cast out and thrown into a land he did not know.
units.Jeremiah 22:29: Land, land, hear the Lord’s word:
units.Jeremiah 22:30: Record this man as an outcast, because no man from his offspring will grow great sitting on David’s throne and ruling again in Judah.
units.Jeremiah 23:1: O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!
units.Jeremiah 23:2: Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.
units.Jeremiah 23:3: And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.
units.Jeremiah 23:4: And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 23:5: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up a righteous rising for David. A king will reign and understand, doing judgment and righteousness upon the earth.
units.Jeremiah 23:6: In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell confidently. This is his name, which the Lord will call him: Josedek.
units.Jeremiah 23:7: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, As the Lord lives, who brought Israel’s house up from Egypt’s land,
units.Jeremiah 23:8: but, As the Lord lives, who gathered all Israel’s offspring from the northern land and all the countries where He drove them out, and restored them to their land.
units.Jeremiah 23:9: Among the prophets my heart was shattered; within me all my bones were shaken. I became like a shattered man, like a person gripped by wine, before the Lord and the splendor of His glory.
units.Jeremiah 23:10: Because of these things the land mourned and the wilderness pastures dried up. Their course became evil, and their strength was not so.
units.Jeremiah 23:11: Because priest and prophet were defiled, and in My house I saw their evils.
units.Jeremiah 23:12: Therefore let their way become a slippery place for them in darkness, and they will be tripped and fall in it, because I will bring evils upon them in their year of visitation, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 23:13: And among Samaria’s prophets I saw lawless acts: they prophesied through Baal and led My people Israel astray.
units.Jeremiah 23:14: And among Jerusalem’s prophets I have seen horrifying things: committing adultery, walking in lies, and supporting evil hands so that no one turns from his evil way. They all became like Sodom to Me, and her inhabitants like Gomorrah.
units.Jeremiah 23:15: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will feed them pain and give them bitter water to drink, because from Jerusalem’s prophets defilement went out into all the land.
units.Jeremiah 23:16: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.
units.Jeremiah 23:17: They say to those rejecting the Lord’s word, You will have peace. To all who walk according to their own wishes, to everyone walking in the wandering of his heart, they said, No evils will come upon you.
units.Jeremiah 23:18: Because who stood in the Lord’s standing place and saw His word? Who gave ear and heard?
units.Jeremiah 23:19: Behold, a shaking comes from the Lord, and anger goes out into a convulsion; swirling, it will come upon the ungodly.
units.Jeremiah 23:20: And the Lord’s fury will no longer turn back until He does it and raises it up from His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days they will understand these things.
units.Jeremiah 23:21: I was not sending the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
units.Jeremiah 23:22: And if they had stood in My standing presence and listened to My words, they would have turned My people from their evil practices.
units.Jeremiah 23:23: I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
units.Jeremiah 23:24: If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 23:25: I heard what the prophets speak, the false things they prophesy in My name, saying, I dreamed a dream.
units.Jeremiah 23:26: How long will it be in the heart of the prophets prophesying false things, and in their prophesying the wishes of their own heart?
units.Jeremiah 23:27: They plan to forget My law through their dreams, which each told his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot My name through Baal.
units.Jeremiah 23:28: Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 23:29: Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?
units.Jeremiah 23:30: Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal My words, each from his neighbor.
units.Jeremiah 23:31: Behold, I am against the prophets who cast out prophecies of the tongue and doze their own dozing.
units.Jeremiah 23:32: Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams, who told them and led My people astray by their lies and wanderings. I did not send or command them, and they will bring this people no benefit at all.
units.Jeremiah 23:33: And if this people, a priest, or a prophet asks you, What is the Lord’s burden? say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 23:34: And the prophet, priest, or people who say, The Lord’s burden—I will exact justice from that person and his household.
units.Jeremiah 23:35: For this is what you will say, each to his neighbor and his brother: What did the Lord answer? What did the Lord speak?
units.Jeremiah 23:36: And do not name the Lord’s burden again, because a person’s own word will be his burden.
units.Jeremiah 23:37: And why did the Lord our God speak?
units.Jeremiah 23:38: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you said this word, The Lord’s burden, though I sent to you saying, Do not say The Lord’s burden,
units.Jeremiah 23:39: therefore behold, I seize you and dash you down, along with the city I gave to you and your fathers,
units.Jeremiah 23:40: and I will put eternal reproach and eternal dishonor upon you, which will not be forgotten.
units.Jeremiah 24:1: The Lord showed me two baskets of figs lying before the Lord’s sanctuary, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, the rulers, craftsmen, prisoners, and rich people from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 24:2: One basket had very good figs, like early figs; the other basket had very bad figs that could not be eaten because of their badness.
units.Jeremiah 24:3: And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Jeremiah? I said: Figs. The good are exceedingly good, and the bad exceedingly bad; they cannot be eaten because of their badness.
units.Jeremiah 24:4: And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
units.Jeremiah 24:5: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Like these good figs, so I will acknowledge Judah’s deportees, whom I have sent from this place to the Chaldeans’ land, for good things.
units.Jeremiah 24:6: And I will fix My eyes upon them for good things and restore them to this land for good things. I will rebuild them and certainly not tear them down, plant them and certainly not pluck them out.
units.Jeremiah 24:7: And I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the Lord. They will be My people and I will be their God, because they will return to Me from their whole heart.
units.Jeremiah 24:8: And like the bad figs that cannot be eaten because of their badness—thus says the Lord—so I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his nobles, Jerusalem’s remnant left in this land, and those dwelling in Egypt.
units.Jeremiah 24:9: And I will give them to scattering into all the earth’s kingdoms, and they will become a reproach, a parable, an object of hatred, and a curse in every place where I drove them out.
units.Jeremiah 24:10: And I will send famine, death, and sword against them until they disappear from the land I gave them.

units.Jeremiah 36:2: after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, and every free person, prisoner, and craftsman left Jerusalem,
units.Jeremiah 36:3: by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon’s king in Babylon, saying:

source_units.text: Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human and will rest the flesh of his arm upon him, and whose heart departs from the Lord;
source_units.complete_text: Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human and will rest the flesh of his arm upon him, and whose heart departs from the Lord;

source_units.text: and he will be like a wild tamarisk in the wilderness; he will not see when good things come, and will dwell among salt-plants and in a wilderness, in a salt land that is not inhabited.
source_units.complete_text: and he will be like a wild tamarisk in the wilderness; he will not see when good things come, and will dwell among salt-plants and in a wilderness, in a salt land that is not inhabited.

source_units.text: And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;
source_units.complete_text: And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;

source_units.text: and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters, and will send its roots toward moisture, and will not fear when heat comes. Wooded stems will be upon it; in a rainless year it will not fear or cease bearing fruit.
source_units.complete_text: and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters, and will send its roots toward moisture, and will not fear when heat comes. Wooded stems will be upon it; in a rainless year it will not fear or cease bearing fruit.

source_units.text: The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?
source_units.complete_text: The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?

source_units.text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
source_units.complete_text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.

source_units.text: A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.
source_units.complete_text: A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.

source_units.text: An exalted throne of glory is our sanctuary,
source_units.complete_text: An exalted throne of glory is our sanctuary,

source_units.text: Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, let all who abandoned Thee be ashamed; let those who departed be written upon the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the fountain of life.
source_units.complete_text: Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, let all who abandoned Thee be ashamed; let those who departed be written upon the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the fountain of life.

source_units.text: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, because Thou art my boast.
source_units.complete_text: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, because Thou art my boast.

source_units.text: Behold, they say to me: Where is the Lord’s word? Let it come!
source_units.complete_text: Behold, they say to me: Where is the Lord’s word? Let it come!

source_units.text: But I did not grow weary following after Thee, and did not desire a human’s day; Thou knowest. The things going out through my lips are before Thee.
source_units.complete_text: But I did not grow weary following after Thee, and did not desire a human’s day; Thou knowest. The things going out through my lips are before Thee.

source_units.text: Do not become an estrangement to me, sparing me in an evil day.
source_units.complete_text: Do not become an estrangement to me, sparing me in an evil day.

source_units.text: Let those pursuing me be ashamed, and may I not be ashamed; may they be terrified, and may I not be terrified. Bring an evil day upon them; crush them with double crushing.
source_units.complete_text: Let those pursuing me be ashamed, and may I not be ashamed; may they be terrified, and may I not be terrified. Bring an evil day upon them; crush them with double crushing.

source_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Go and stand in the gates of your people’s sons, through which Judah’s kings enter and leave, and in all Jerusalem’s gates,
source_units.complete_text: Thus says the Lord: Go and stand in the gates of your people’s sons, through which Judah’s kings enter and leave, and in all Jerusalem’s gates,

source_units.text: and you will say to them: Hear the Lord’s word, kings of Judah, all Judea and all Jerusalem, who enter these gates:
source_units.complete_text: and you will say to them: Hear the Lord’s word, kings of Judah, all Judea and all Jerusalem, who enter these gates:

source_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Guard your souls, and do not lift burdens on the Sabbath day or go out through Jerusalem’s gates,
source_units.complete_text: Thus says the Lord: Guard your souls, and do not lift burdens on the Sabbath day or go out through Jerusalem’s gates,

source_units.text: and do not bring burdens out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and you must do no work; consecrate the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers. And they did not hear or incline their ear,
source_units.complete_text: and do not bring burdens out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and you must do no work; consecrate the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers. And they did not hear or incline their ear,

source_units.text: and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers, so as not to hear Me or accept instruction.
source_units.complete_text: and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers, so as not to hear Me or accept instruction.

source_units.text: And if you truly listen to Me, says the Lord, not bringing burdens through this city’s gates on the Sabbath day and consecrating the Sabbath day by doing no work,
source_units.complete_text: And if you truly listen to Me, says the Lord, not bringing burdens through this city’s gates on the Sabbath day and consecrating the Sabbath day by doing no work,

source_units.text: then kings and rulers sitting on David’s throne will enter through this city’s gates, mounted on their chariots and horses, they and their rulers, Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited for ever.
source_units.complete_text: then kings and rulers sitting on David’s throne will enter through this city’s gates, mounted on their chariots and horses, they and their rulers, Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited for ever.

source_units.text: And they will come from Judah’s cities, around Jerusalem, Benjamin’s land, the plain, the mountain and the south, bringing whole burnt offerings, sacrifice, incense offerings, grain offering and frankincense, bringing praise into the Lord’s house.
source_units.complete_text: And they will come from Judah’s cities, around Jerusalem, Benjamin’s land, the plain, the mountain and the south, bringing whole burnt offerings, sacrifice, incense offerings, grain offering and frankincense, bringing praise into the Lord’s house.

source_units.text: And if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day, not lifting burdens and not entering Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle fire in her gates, and it will devour Jerusalem’s quarters and not be extinguished.
source_units.complete_text: And if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day, not lifting burdens and not entering Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle fire in her gates, and it will devour Jerusalem’s quarters and not be extinguished.

source_units.text: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
source_units.complete_text: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:

source_units.text: Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.
source_units.complete_text: Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.

source_units.text: And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones.
source_units.complete_text: And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones.

source_units.text: And the vessel he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as pleased him to make.
source_units.complete_text: And the vessel he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as pleased him to make.

source_units.text: And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
source_units.complete_text: And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:

source_units.text: Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands.
source_units.complete_text: Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands.

source_units.text: At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,
source_units.complete_text: At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,

source_units.text: and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.
source_units.complete_text: and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.

source_units.text: And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,
source_units.complete_text: And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,

source_units.text: and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.
source_units.complete_text: and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.

source_units.text: And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.
source_units.complete_text: And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.

source_units.text: And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.
source_units.complete_text: And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.

source_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among the nations: Who heard such horrifying things that virgin Israel committed so greatly?
source_units.complete_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among the nations: Who heard such horrifying things that virgin Israel committed so greatly?

source_units.text: Will breasts fail from a rock, or snow from Lebanon? Will water borne violently by wind turn aside?
source_units.complete_text: Will breasts fail from a rock, or snow from Lebanon? Will water borne violently by wind turn aside?

source_units.text: Because My people forgot Me, they burned incense in vain; and they will become weak in their ways, the age-old tracks, to step upon paths having no road for travel,
source_units.complete_text: Because My people forgot Me, they burned incense in vain; and they will become weak in their ways, the age-old tracks, to step upon paths having no road for travel,

source_units.text: to make their land a ruin and an eternal hissing; all who pass through it will be astonished and shake their head.
source_units.complete_text: to make their land a ruin and an eternal hissing; all who pass through it will be astonished and shake their head.

source_units.text: Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them their day of destruction.
source_units.complete_text: Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them their day of destruction.

source_units.text: And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.
source_units.complete_text: And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.

source_units.text: Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.
source_units.complete_text: Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.

source_units.text: Is evil repaid for good things? For they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me. Remember my standing before Thee to speak good things for them, to turn Thy fury from them.
source_units.complete_text: Is evil repaid for good things? For they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me. Remember my standing before Thee to speak good things for them, to turn Thy fury from them.

source_units.text: Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.
source_units.complete_text: Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.

source_units.text: Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.
source_units.complete_text: Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.

source_units.text: And Thou, Lord, knewest all their counsel against me for death. Do not acquit their injustices or erase their sins from before Thee. Let their weakness be before Thee; act among them in the time of Thy fury.
source_units.complete_text: And Thou, Lord, knewest all their counsel against me for death. Do not acquit their injustices or erase their sins from before Thee. Let their weakness be before Thee; act among them in the time of Thy fury.

source_units.complete_text: And go out to the burial ground of the sons of their children, which is before the Charsith Gate, and read there all the words that I speak to you.

source_units.complete_text: And I will make this city a ruin and a hissing. Everyone passing through it will look gloomy and hiss over its whole wound.

source_units.complete_text: and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.

source_units.complete_text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon this city, all its towns, and its villages all the evils I spoke against it, because they hardened their necks so as not to listen to My words.

source_units.complete_text: And he struck him and put him into the trap, which was at the gate of the separated upper house that was in the Lord’s house.

source_units.complete_text: And Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the trap, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has called your name not Pashhur but Migrant.

source_units.complete_text: And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.

source_units.complete_text: And you and all who dwell in your house will go into captivity. In Babylon you will die and there be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.

source_units.complete_text: Thou didst deceive me, Lord, and I was deceived. Thou tookest hold and didst prevail. I became a laughingstock; all day I continued being mocked.

source_units.complete_text: Because I will laugh with my bitter word; I will call upon rejection and misery, because the Lord’s word became a reproach and a derision to me all day long.

source_units.text: Because I heard the reproach of many gathering all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all you men who are his friends! Watch his purpose, to see whether he will be deceived and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.
source_units.complete_text: Because I heard the reproach of many gathering all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all you men who are his friends! Watch his purpose, to see whether he will be deceived and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.

source_units.text: And the Lord is with me like a strong fighter. Therefore they pursued and could not understand; they were greatly shamed, because they did not understand their dishonors, which will never be forgotten.
source_units.complete_text: And the Lord is with me like a strong fighter. Therefore they pursued and could not understand; they were greatly shamed, because they did not understand their dishonors, which will never be forgotten.

source_units.complete_text: Lord, testing righteous things, understanding kidneys and hearts: May I see the vengeance from Thee among them, because to Thee I disclosed my defenses.

source_units.text: Sing to the Lord; praise Him, because He rescued a poor person’s life from the hand of those doing evil.
source_units.complete_text: Sing to the Lord; praise Him, because He rescued a poor person’s life from the hand of those doing evil.

source_units.complete_text: Accursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day my mother bore me not be a day to pray for!

source_units.complete_text: Accursed be the man who brought my father good news, saying, A boy has been born to you!—rejoicing.

source_units.complete_text: because he did not kill me in my mother’s womb, so that my mother would have become my tomb and the womb one of everlasting conception.

source_units.complete_text: Why did I come out from the womb to see labors and pains, and have my days continue in shame?

source_units.complete_text: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:

source_units.complete_text: Ask the Lord about us, because Babylon’s king has come against us, whether the Lord will act according to all His wonders, so that he goes away from us.

source_units.complete_text: And Jeremiah said to them: Say this to Zedekiah king of Judah:

source_units.complete_text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am turning the weapons of war with which you fight the Chaldeans who have shut you in outside the wall into this city,

source_units.complete_text: and I Myself will fight you with outstretched hand and mighty arm, with fury, anger, and great indignation.

source_units.complete_text: And I will strike all this city’s inhabitants, the people and the livestock, with a great death, and they will die.

source_units.complete_text: Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.

source_units.complete_text: House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.

source_units.complete_text: Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Sor, the level land, you who say, Who will frighten us? Or who will enter our dwelling?

source_units.complete_text: And I will kindle a fire in her woodland, and it will consume everything around her.

source_units.complete_text: and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.

source_units.complete_text: Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.

source_units.complete_text: Because thus says the Lord against the house of Judah’s king: You are Gilead to Me, the head of Lebanon; surely I will make you a wilderness, cities that will not be inhabited.

source_units.complete_text: And I will bring against you a destroying man and his axe, and they will cut down your chosen cedars and cast them into the fire.

source_units.complete_text: And nations will pass through this city, and each will say to his neighbor: Why did the Lord act this way toward this great city?

source_units.complete_text: And they will say: Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down to foreign gods, and served them.

source_units.complete_text: Do not weep for the dead or lament him; weep bitterly for the one going out, because he will never return or see his homeland.

source_units.complete_text: but in the place where I deported him, there he will die, and he will never see this land again.

source_units.complete_text: Will you reign because you are provoked in Ahaz your father? They will not eat or drink. It was better for you to do judgment and good righteousness.

source_units.complete_text: They did not know; they did not judge a case for the lowly or a case for the poor. Is this not your failing to know Me? says the Lord.

source_units.complete_text: Behold, neither your eyes nor your heart are good; instead they are directed toward your greed, innocent blood to shed it, wrongdoing, and murder to commit it.

source_units.complete_text: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: Woe upon this man! They will certainly not mourn him, O brother! Nor will they weep for him, Alas, lord!

source_units.complete_text: Jeconiah was dishonored like a vessel for which there is no use, because he was cast out and thrown into a land he did not know.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related adverse outcomes of unjustly acquired wealth
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah joins wealth made without judgment to abandonment in the middle of the possessor's days and final foolishness; Proverbs says property pursued with lawlessness diminishes. Proverbs does not reproduce the partridge image or Jeremiah's timing in the middle of the person's days.
final_amended_triples.source_text: A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.

target_units.text: Property pursued eagerly with lawlessness becomes less, but one who gathers for himself with piety will increase; a righteous person has compassion and lends.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close hardened-neck refusal to hear inherited commandments
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes a neck hardened beyond the fathers and refusal to hear or accept instruction. The confession in Nehemiah likewise joins the fathers' stiffened necks with refusal to hear God's commandments.
final_amended_triples.source_text: and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers, so as not to hear Me or accept instruction.

target_units.text: “But they and our fathers acted arrogantly, stiffened their necks and did not listen to Thy commandments.

“They refused to listen and did not remember Thy wonders that Thou hadst done among them. They stiffened their necks and appointed leadership to return to their slavery in Egypt. But Thou art a merciful and compassionate God, longsuffering and abundant in mercy, and Thou didst not abandon them.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related warning and account of Jerusalem's burning
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah threatens unquenched fire consuming Jerusalem's quarters if Sabbath instructions are rejected. Chronicles records the burning of Jerusalem's citadels and the sanctuary, then relates the desolation to the land's Sabbaths and Jeremiah's word; it does not identify this individual warning as its sole referenced prediction.
final_amended_triples.source_text: And if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day, not lifting burdens and not entering Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle fire in her gates, and it will devour Jerusalem’s quarters and not be extinguished.

target_units.text: He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.
He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related reversal through subsequent wrongdoing
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah says a nation that does evil and refuses God's voice may lose the announced good. Ezekiel likewise says a person who trusts in his righteousness but commits lawlessness will die; the comparison distinguishes the national and individual settings.
final_amended_triples.source_text: and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.

target_units.text: When I speak to the righteous man—this one has trusted in his righteousness, yet commits lawlessness—none of his righteous deeds will ever be remembered. In the injustice he committed, in it he will die.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close refusal expressed as following the evil heart
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah 18 reports the people's determination to follow their turnings away and what pleases each evil heart. Jeremiah 7 likewise describes refusal to listen and following the thoughts of their evil heart.
final_amended_triples.source_text: And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.

target_units.text: And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, but they walked in the thoughts of their evil heart and went backward rather than forward.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related divine scattering expressed through wind imagery
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares the people's scattering before enemies to a scorching wind. Ezekiel says God will scatter a portion of Jerusalem's people to every wind; the passages share divine dispersion without making the winds' descriptions identical.
final_amended_triples.source_text: Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them their day of destruction.

target_units.text: A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related judgment upon those concealing traps
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks for a cry in their houses and anticipates sudden robbers upon people who planned his capture and hid traps. The psalm describes an unjustly concealed trap and asks that the hidden snare catch those who set it.
final_amended_triples.source_text: Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.

target_units.text: For without cause they hid for me the destruction of their trap; without purpose they reproached my soul.
Let a trap they do not know come upon them; let the snare they hid catch them, and into that trap they will fall.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close desolation and dismayed passersby
final_amended_triples.rationale: Both portray a devastated place drawing a dismayed response from everyone passing through. Chapter 19 specifies the city and its wound; chapter 18 speaks of the land, astonishment and shaking heads.
final_amended_triples.source_text: And I will make this city a ruin and a hissing. Everyone passing through it will look gloomy and hiss over its whole wound.

target_units.text: to make their land a ruin and an eternal hissing; all who pass through it will be astonished and shake their head.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related reproach incurred through association with God
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah says the Lord's word became reproach and derision to him. The psalm says reproaches directed at God fell upon the speaker; this comparison concerns transferred reproach and does not paraphrase Jeremiah's unusual opening as a cry against violence.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close appeal to God's inward knowledge for vindication
final_amended_triples.rationale: Both appeals ask to see God's vengeance upon opponents because the speaker disclosed his defense or claim of right to Him. final_amended_triples.rationale: The house of David is commanded to set judgment straight and rescue the plundered. The psalm for Solomon asks righteous royal judgment and describes the king saving the children of the needy and humbling the false accuser.

final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah's concluding judgment says doing judgment and good righteousness was better for the royal addressee. target_units.text: A righteous king raises up a country, but a lawless man tears it down.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related lament over shattered or faithless lovers
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah's address calls for lament because all the lovers have been shattered. Lamentations describes Jerusalem without comfort among her lovers and with faithless friends turned enemies; it does not say those lovers themselves were shattered.
final_amended_triples.source_text: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan and shout to the far side of the sea, because all your lovers have been shattered.

final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares the coming pangs of the cedar-nesting addressee to a woman giving birth. Micah addresses Zion with the same birth-pang image and expressly connects it with leaving the city for Babylon.

final_amended_triples.rationale: The oracle predicts that Jeconiah and his mother will die in the foreign land to which God casts them. final_amended_triples.relationship: related direct summons to the earth to hear
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah addresses the land twice and commands it to hear the Lord's word. Moses' song likewise addresses the earth as a hearer of his words, together with heaven; the scope and repeated wording differ.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close gathering of scattered people into pasture
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah promises to receive the remnant from the lands of dispersion and establish them in pasture. Ezekiel likewise promises gathering from countries into Israel's land and good pasture, using the same restored-flock imagery.
final_amended_triples.source_text: And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.

target_units.text: I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.

final_amended_triples.relationship: close rejection of prophecy originating in the speaker's own heart
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah warns against prophetic words from the prophets' own hearts rather than the Lord's mouth. Ezekiel likewise condemns prophets speaking from their own heart while seeing nothing at all.
final_amended_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.

final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah says the prophets ran though God did not send them and prophesied though He did not speak. Ezekiel similarly condemns those saying The Lord says although the Lord has not sent them.

final_amended_triples.relationship: related faithful ministry turning people from injustice
final_amended_triples.rationale: Jeremiah says prophets who truly stood before God and heard Him would have turned the people from evil practices. Malachi presents truthful priestly speech and the turning of many from injustice as the positive counterpart.

The passages introduce different prophetic messages within this shared named setting.
